newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Hepworth hit by redundancy, pensions.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hepworth hit by redundancy, pensions.

text.p: British heating and building materials group Hepworth Plc said on Thursday redundancy and pension costs dragged down profits in 1996 and warned the strong pound and rising pension costs could eat into earnings this year.

"1997 will be a challenging year as sterling's recent rise against major European currencies will impact translation of overseas earnings...a further increase in the pension charge will also impact earnings," Hepworth said.
Hepworth said pretax profits dropped 9.3 percent last year to 67.6 million pounds ($110.1 million), hit by redundancy costs of 6.7 million as the group strove to slash its cost base.

Pension charges rose 58 percent to 5.7 million pounds and sterling's strength and a goodwill write-off of 7.5 million resulted in equity shareholders' funds being cut 2.6 percent to 213.2 million, the company said.
Hepworth shares showed little reaction to the figures, which were in line with analysts' expectations. The stock was down 1-1/2 pence at 257-12p in early morning trade in London.
Hepworth said sales rose 1.6 percent last year to 777.8 million pounds, helped by rising exports and recent acquisitions. The company proposed paying an unchanged dividend of 14.85 pence.

Hepworth, pledging "vigorous" action to cut its cost base further this year, said however the underlying outlook was positive, with signs of modest recovery in the British construction and home improvement markets. It said its continental heating operations were also seeing firmer demand.
Hepworth, which said in October last year it was holding talks on the possible sale of its Refractories Division, said discussions were continuing but it gave no further details.
In 1996 turnover at the division dropped 3.6 percent to 157.1 million pounds and profits slipped marginally to 7.4 million, weighed down by 3.0 million pounds redundancy and rationalisation costs.
Hepworth said the Refractories Division's most important market -- European steel -- saw production fall six percent although British steel demand was stable and production rose three percent.

The group's French heating business Hepworth Saunier Duval raised sales and profits in franc terms last year but profit in sterling terms dropped 2.4 percent to 28.3 million pounds. Volumes were hit by its withdrawal from the home improvement market.

At Hepworth Building Products, sales dropped slightly to 168.4 million pounds but operating profits slid 28 percent to 11.6 million, hit primarily by increased competition in the German clay pipe market and industrial overcapacity.
Hepworth Home Products saw turnover rise 17 percent to 132.4 million pounds, helped by higher sales of gas boilers by Hepworth Heating, the company said.

Hepworth said the lacklustre German vehicle industry had hit sales of foundry sand at Hepworth Minerals and Chemicals. It said volumes in the British glass market were "generally subdued" and demand from the building sector slipped significantly.
However, exports outside Europe gained 17 percent and Hepworth said markets in the Far East looked promising. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
